newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia govt unaware PSC project shelved.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia govt unaware PSC project shelved.

text.p: Malaysia's Defence Minister said on Monday he was unaware that a multi-billion ringgit offshore patrol vessel (OPV) project to be carried out by PSC Industries Bhd had been cancelled.

"I don't know anything about such a cancellation, neither does the military chief, probably the newspaper knows more than us," Syed Hamid Albar told reporters after talks with visiting French Defence Minister Charles Millon.

The Sun daily, quoting a "well-informed source", said on Monday the government was postponing the project after studying its financial implications and its adverse impact on the country's current account deficit.
"As far as the Malaysian government is concerned, the purchase of the 27 OPVs under the privatisation of the LNDSB (Lumut Naval Dockyard Sdn Bhd) is on.
"A lot of questions have been asked whether it has been shelved. It's not. It's a five billion ringgit programme over 15 years," Syed Hamid said.
At a separate news conference, PSC Industries Bhd said it too was not aware of the project having been postponed.
"As far as we are concerned, the project is still on," PSC chairman Amin Shah Omar Shah told reporters.
